column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3c context: a range is the more careful form, not the usual one (8 of 20 posted reports); Keel's tally, not a survey.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and Table 2 note; 19.0% checks ($20,000 over a $105,000 midpoint; NUMBERS 4's stated $95,000-$115,000) and so do the 22.2-50% widths, but 'narrower than any range a consultant gave a board' is false inside this card: Spooner's report also states 8.7% (row 13) and Howard County's whole campaign with its committed $25M is 5.9% (row 15), the like-for-like shape; say narrower than all eight ranges of money not yet offered.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c aha: counsel gives confidence only in words; after the move Laura can say certain because both ends are owned (NUMBERS 4).
Mon 16 Nov: 3c: practitioners already treat a range as a firm bottom and a hoped-for top, Laura's shape before the move (IPS l.15).
Mon 16 Nov: 3c/3d: a board's confidence is a poll of opinions about money not yet given; one clause at most beside row 3.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: ask high, then cut; close to H9-129's working goal.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d beside aha 8: at feasibility a board has only 10-53% of its goal offered, so most of its range is money not yet given; the conceit's contrast in numbers (CONCEIT V2).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: fundraisers also round a stated goal down; matches NUMBERS 4's rounding to $5,000.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c/3d: a real report's baseline and stretch, reassessed before going public, is Laura's order (2.9-10.7% checks with NUMBERS 4); one parish, so one clause.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d wording: 'at least' is counsel's word while the top is unknown; supports rows 31-33 against NUMBERS 4 option D.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b/3d: a public rule for money above the stated top; Laura's excess ($8,476) joins the half kept (NUMBERS 4; CANON D12).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d contrast: a feasible bottom missed and the building cut; the shortfall is mostly a bond vote, so say so.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: three ranges in one report read as soft; also why row 2's 'narrower than every range' needs care.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d context: campaign pledges arrive over three years; Laura's money is owned first (IPS l.15).
Mon 16 Nov: 3c/3d: the closest public shape to Laura's (a committed nucleus plus a range on top); its 5.9% whole-campaign width is the fair comparison for row 2.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: counsel's own methods differ by 70%.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a leader's hopes push a figure up; a letter to parishioners, not co-funders.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c: campaigns average 106-116% of goal, worst 75%; 107.4% checks ($123,476 over $115,000, NUMBERS 4) but that excess joins her flexibility, not the facility (CANON D12), so lead with the floor of outcomes: their worst is 75% of goal, her contribution equals the stated top in every path.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: the sample shapes the lesson; not causal.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a smaller goal against what is in hand matters more than a study; 2005 and local.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d beside aha 8: a large arts campaign went public at 92% committed; one campaign, so aha 8's 60-80% stays the norm.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c: the setup for row 23, a floor and a range hung on one share price.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c/3e aha: the best-known 'at least' arts gift sat in one share and lost $102M in a year despite a draft IPS; Laura's bottom is a Treasury fund; tell with row 24's recovery so it is not read as cherry-picked.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c: the share floor came good only after a lawsuit; say her floor's payout cannot fall after January 2028, not that it never has a bad year (the fund's price can move).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: conflicting figures from different dates; context for row 23.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b/3e: a Taiwan founder's figure outrun by a building and topped up, IPS l.15's overruns; never imply her flexibility covers a top-up of that size (aha 8's fix); pledge amount conflicting.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a fixed donor figure while the state carried the rise; in Taiwan the founder pays first and grantees carry overruns (row 30), so never suggest co-sponsors carry hers.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a fixed founder figure, then more as a separate choice (CANON D12).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d conceit contrast: promises stated as a share of future wealth were kept 8 times in 22; an advocacy think tank's count, so name it.
Mon 16 Nov: Twin of Q11e-016 (overruns borne by the grantee; multi-year grants cut with the budget); the no-compensation clause can be added there.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d wording: 'at least n' leaves about half of readers doubting an exact n; Geurts and Nouwen read only through Cummins and Katsos.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d: from a speaker who knows, 'at least' signals ignorance and hints at money CANON D12 keeps outside; argues against NUMBERS 4 option D.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d: the bare figure says exactly; 'at least' fits only a how-much-at-minimum question asked before the top is known.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: counsel shows its record; Laura's is the rule's record (both ends owned in every history window after the move, NUMBERS 4).
Mon 16 Nov: 3a/3d, a conceit turn: a national funder calls its own later years 'indicative'; Laura's ten are owned and dated (NUMBERS 8h).
Mon 16 Nov: Twin of Q55-001 (the same funder's 'indicative' later years); the over-1m-a-year line is its detail.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: long public relationships built one budget at a time.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: payment mechanics; Laura's is one dated sum a year (8h cash dates).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Australia's four-year funding; Australia only if it earns its place.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e: a four-year promise ends in a cliff with no transition; Laura's end (2042) is dated from the start.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d: a funder scores confirmed future funding as capacity; say proof the residency can run, never that it qualifies for public support or is an anchor or match (SKELETON 3d); an Australian funder.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d: verifies Q9c-011: NCAF approves year one only and earmarks later years; pair with row 9 in one clause.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d's half-clause (pays one year at a time) and a conceit turn: NCAF may cut pro rata or stop every later year.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d evidence clause: 5 of 93 top Taiwan troupes held any multi-year operating promise, at most three years; use this or Q9c's clause, not both.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a funder's own money covered a budget trim; $35,894 matches NUMBERS 2 and 8h; never a recession cut (CANON B4).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d scale: $50,000 is about NT$1.64m at 32.768 (8d), inside NCAF's NT$1m-8m band; the rate moves (8j).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d scale: Taiwan's visual-arts operating grants average about NT$714,000; Laura's is over twice that for ten years; a nearer analogue than row 12.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d wording: even unrestricted multi-year letters gate later years and may stop; Laura's letter can say will be paid.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a leadership change can stop a funder's later payments; same point as row 14.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d wording: big funders write 'expected'; Laura can write will be paid because each payment is bought.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d: one 'no conditions' line lets the residency count the ten; adds drafting practice to Q18-001 to Q18-003.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a/3d: only 12.4% of grants are both multi-year and operating support; US and pre-2020.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Exponent's figures only as CEP quotes them; read the report before use.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a aha: a quarter of willing foundation leaders hold back because precommitting funds is risky; Laura bought first (IPS l.13); the survey is about large unrestricted gifts, say so.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a funding cliff is funders' first worry; recipients save into reserves.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: a model funder's later years rode on its investments and shrank; Laura's ride on no share price (IPS l.11).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d: arts groups ask for five to seven years; supports row 45.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d scale: $50,000 a year is what MacArthur gives a $1m-budget arts group, for three years, not ten.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: twenty years built from four renewals; what is promised on day one differs.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a/3d: the longest fixed arts schedule found is seven years, to individuals; supports row 45.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: BUILD's five-year term; the $1.85 million slip unconfirmed.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a/3b: steady money lets a grantee build its own reserve, which Q9 and Q9b tie to survival; self-report.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e: not knowing the end hurt planning more each year; Laura's last payment is dated from 2027.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e: say the end at the start; one clause on what follows 2042 (8k), since Wharton's monitoring runs to 2033.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: long funders exit by choice; fix the citation: the two reasons are IPS l.17, not l.19.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: dated payments are each year's support in the residency's books, the ladder's shape (IPS l.13).
Mon 16 Nov: 3a/2.3: an auditor values a promise by the giver's creditworthiness; Laura's answer is Treasuries, not her career (IPS l.11).
Mon 16 Nov: Twin of H3-109 (an unconditional pledge is booked at once); the schedule-alone point can be added there.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: Taiwan gift law is out of scope (case A13); context for one clause at most.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: periodic gifts lapse at death unless stated; case A13; Laura's age and health never raised.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: the livelihood defence; Keel inference; case A13.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a notarial deed gives the right and Treasuries the assets; case A13; a secondary law-firm note.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: verifies Salsbury (Q18-028, merged into H3-109) and adds that executors may wait for a court.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a second state's pledge test; specific sums and dates make a promise usable.
Mon 16 Nov: Twin of Q18-031 (a DAF route turns a promise into an intention); note IPS l.19 does not say the Treasuries stay hers (l.17 makes them the reserve).

Mon 16 Nov: 3a clause beside H3-069: the tax code's test of a guaranteed stream (a determinable amount, at least yearly, a fixed term) is met by the ten without a trust; fix the citation: IPS l.19 says nothing about keeping them, use l.17.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a: 'only the ten sit in owned and promised' is wrong: after the move the stated range is owned in Treasuries and promised too (NUMBERS 4); the half kept is owned in shares, which the conceit calls pencil, so the ink square means owned in Treasuries; no new exhibit (four stay).
Mon 16 Nov: 3d/3e list: amounts, dates, no conditions, the schedule, 111.4% (checks with 8h) and what follows 2042 stand; drop the notarised deed, which is advice on Taiwan law (case A13).
Mon 16 Nov: 3a/3d one line: no arts funder read fixes more than seven years and Laura's ten are owned; programmes read, not a census.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c context only: 'checked before take-off' maps loosely to stating after the move; the 2.9/6.2/8.7/10.7% match NUMBERS 4.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: interest on cash waiting as unusable fuel; fees match NUMBERS 0 and 2; say cash waiting, since every coupon still counts (8h's definition).

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0/3a: each margin's job matches NUMBERS (the 0.5% for costs beyond the two fees; the extra Treasuries for zero interest, $45,456 back on 1 Jan 2033 at forwards; her flexibility for IPS l.15's three uses), but the three guard three promises (the ten, the stated ends, the building), not one flight, and no final reserve sits under the design test ($0 left at 0% with the ETF fee), so drop 'her bound plays that role'; evidence, never a second image.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c: both round toward safety; $98,380 to $95,000 and $118,072 to $115,000 match NUMBERS 4.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b: 'the extra Treasuries never fund the facility' is not in NUMBERS: what comes back from them is Laura's (8k) and may reach the building as her separate choice (CANON D12); say they never count toward the stated range.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and Table 3: watch and act in fixed words; matches IPS l.17's two reasons and Table 3's notice watch; SKELETON 3e already has the tiers, so this is outside evidence; no aviation words in Table 3.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e: one clause at most beside row 6; competes with the conceit's 3e turn (registration marks).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: fixed names must be used one way every time (WORDS).

Mon 16 Nov: 3c: the 0.5% is itself a round figure checked against the ended funds' costs (about 0.27%, NUMBERS 0, card Q3c), not set from data as EASA's statistical fuel is; say checked against evidence, never sized on evidence.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: a release passes the test that sized it (8h's release test counts future flows at zero); Keel's reading, IPS silent.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b: her flexibility has no rule-set size, Caplet's choice (Q5b, 8o); the parallel is the owner's discretion only, as its disanalogy says; never the best split.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c: the setup for rows 13-14 (a line that recorded what the owner intended).

Mon 16 Nov: 3c aha: a mark means nothing when the one who gains can move it; the range rule is fixed before it gives a figure and both ends are owned after the move; cite Glover for the derision, the funnel story is 'apparently'.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c/3d: say from tables, not intentions (each holding's zero-interest payout); never imply an outside authority sets or enforces Laura's rule (it is the team's written rule, card Q19), as the disanalogy admits.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a closed list of exceptions, like IPS l.17's two reasons.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a voluntary rule was ignored; it cuts both ways, since Laura's rule is voluntary too.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: $5,300 of flexibility per $5,000 of top matches 8o; never imply misconduct.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d: a mark anyone can check; co-sponsors can check holdings by CUSIP and ticker (Table 1, card Q38).
Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 note at most: 111.4% ($444,545 against $399,089) matches 8h; form only, never beside NERC's 15%.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c: the floor is counted at what its holdings pay with no interest after the two fees, less 0.5% (NUMBERS 3), not at net asset value less costs; VT at zero gives $95,000 (NUMBERS 4) checks.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: a probability margin misses the common shock; the 585 windows follow from the bound (NUMBERS 2), so never offer them as separate proof (aha 5's fix).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: the cost lands on people who never chose the risk.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a/3c: 'contractually pay' is wrong for the iBond funds, which seek no predetermined amount; say counted at what their holdings pay with no interest earned, less 0.5%; never call a fund's payout fixed.
Mon 16 Nov: Twin of Q8a-010 (graver consequence, stricter standard); row 26 carries the dam point for 3b.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a aha: a fraction of the bound is not a standard; $22,192 and 35 of 585 match NUMBERS 2; but only the $2,388 top-up is IPS l.13's completion clause: the extra Treasuries ($35,894) rest on l.13's 'not dependent on yields staying put', never 'inside the completion clause' for the $38,282 (WORDS; INTENT failure 7).

Mon 16 Nov: 3b aha: the standard follows who carries the loss; the payments reach the residency's people, a fall in her flexibility lands on her; the stalled-facility disanalogy does not break it, since the stated top is owned before it is stated.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: freeboard as the gap above the design case; Q47's trim and safe area cover the stated top.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: the No-margin row ($125,000-$155,000) matches NUMBERS 4, but a 2,209-death disaster beside one open sizing call (Keel's, Tue 10 Nov) is the wrong tone, and the margin was never spent a little at a time.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a/3e: the backstop is the same instruments as the rungs, and the payout path has run five times (IBTA 15 days early, card Q3c); common cause stays the named exception.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: $8,813 and $58,603 released, 113.0% to 248.2% kept, all match 8h; Keel's reading, IPS silent.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: $1,180 compares the fee-cushioned $336,656 with $337,836 sized without the fee; NUMBERS 2's like-for-like is $335,771 against $337,836, $2,065 dearer.
Mon 16 Nov: Twin of Q5c-024 (one pot cannot back two promises); one holder of all margins adds little.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.0/3c: measured, calculated and estimated numbers draw the ink and pencil line (bonds and the funds' zero-interest payouts owned, VT pencil until moved); a fact under the conceit, never a second image.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: policed words, like WORDS' fixed names.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: heritage parts need less margin; read through the Air Force tailoring only.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e context: why the plan never claims her flexibility covers any overrun; mass is not money.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: $13,220 more and the floor payout $115,929 to $103,178 match NUMBERS 2; Apollo adds little beyond stating the price plainly.
Mon 16 Nov: Twin of Q5-003 (estimate plus contingency set at a 50% chance of overrun); the two-to-three-times and currency notes can be added there.

Mon 16 Nov: 3.0/3a aha: the plan's biggest margin is expected back ($45,456 on 1 Jan 2033 at forwards, 8h) and its smallest, the 0.5%, partly spent; matches NUMBERS; say the two guard different promises.

Mon 16 Nov: References: Graham's motto bridges to the investing literature; ch. 20 may apply it to bonds as earnings over fixed charges, nearer Laura than price below value: check in the book; the 'accurate estimate' line stays UNVERIFIED.
Mon 16 Nov: 3.0/3e: four marks of a margin that holds; too long for one sentence, use one mark at a time.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a: the margin guards interest on every waiting dollar from 2027 (coupons worth $93,941 by 2033, NUMBERS 2), not only the principal waits named; H8-104 already holds the zero-rate line.
